nodes.long_description:
Your house just became a shoot house.

Build & Breach turns your living room, garage, backyard, or office into a full room-clearing CQB mission in seconds. Stack on a real door, pie the corner, and breach. Nobody knows what's waiting on the other side. Not even you.

BUILD IT. Drop walls, doors, furniture, and people anywhere in your space, or let Fish Bowl throw a brand-new random house at you every round. Design bigger layouts in the free Builder desktop app.

RUN IT.
• Hostiles who fight back from cover, fake surrenders who turn on you, and civilians who panic, hide, or beg.
• Yell "Hands up!" and watch them comply. Voice commands run right on your headset.
• Kill the lights and go in with night vision.
• Rounds tear through drywall and wood. Brick will save you.
• Eight weapons, real attachments, and limited mags. Count your rounds.

REVIEW IT. Every run ends with an After Action Report and a score. Climb your Training Record, crank the difficulty, and go again.

No range. No facility. No excuses.

Requires Meta Quest 3 or 3S. Mixed reality: clear your play space first.

BUILD & BREACH

 TRAIN ANYWHERE, ANYTIME.
nodes.short_description: Build & Breach is a mixed-reality CQB simulator that turns your real-world space into a customizable virtual shoot house. Build rooms, place doors and furniture, and clear AI threats inside your own home.

nodes.long_description:
​​BUILD & BREACH CQB is a mixed-reality close-quarters battle (CQB) simulator that lets you design and clear tactical environments inside your real-world space.
Using passthrough mixed reality, you can place walls, doors, furniture, and obstacles directly into your physical environment to create custom CQB layouts. Every object is anchored to the real world using spatial anchors, meaning your rooms stay locked in place even if you remove the headset or hand it to another user. This allows multiple people to experience the exact same scenario in the same physical space.
Before each run, you build the battlefield. Design tight hallways, doorways, and room layouts to create realistic clearing challenges. When the scenario begins, hostile AI units populate the environment and engage you as you move through your physical space. Enemies take cover, react to movement, and force you to clear rooms methodically using proper angles, positioning, and timing.
Weapons feature realistic handling, requiring you to aim, reload, and manage your firearm under pressure. Every doorway is dangerous, every corner matters, and no two runs play the same.
Build & Breach is built for CQB enthusiasts who want a serious, immersive close-quarters battle sandbox that turns their own environment into the battlefield.
Build it.
Breach it.
Clear it.
nodes.short_description: Build & Breach is a mixed-reality CQB simulator that lets you turn your real-world space into a fully customizable combat environment with Mixed Reality. Design rooms, place doors and furniture, and run dynamic clearing drills against AI threats — all inside your own home.

# Build & Breach 3.1.31 — release notes (production build)

**Fish Bowl brief:** page 2 (Rules of Engagement) no longer runs into the CONTINUE button.
**Grenades:** switched on and off from the LOADOUT's GRENADE card only; the duplicate SETTINGS row is gone.
**Fix:** hovering some menu icons no longer throws an error in the background.

# Build & Breach 3.1.30 — release notes

**Tutorial VOICE tab:** the main-menu tutorial lists every voice command the game understands, grouped by what it does, with tips on who hears you.
**Full vest every round:** every rifle and pistol pouch is refilled when a round starts, including pouches that were hidden or rebuilt (after a loadout change) between rounds.
**All guns included:** this store build ships every weapon free (no add-on lock).

# Build & Breach 3.1.28 — release notes

**3.1.20 – 3.1.28** (since the 3.1.19 alpha candidate):

**Magazines are finite:** three rifle mags on the vest and two pistol mags on the support hip, one per pouch per round, refilled at every countdown. Put a part-used mag back in an empty pouch to keep it. The intro tutorial keeps endless mags.
**SHOOTING HAND** setting (RIGHT / LEFT): the holster and grenade go on your side, the pistol mags on the other.
**Intro tutorial:** seven stations. Station 3 TALK THEM DOWN teaches voice commands ("HANDS UP!" → "GET DOWN!") and station 7 LIGHTS OUT is a night-vision room. The left menu button shows the station's instructions beside RESUME / END SCENARIO.
**TRAINING RECORD** (home ▸ RECORD): every graded round with a COMPLEXITY rating (hostiles by type, innocents, rooms to clear, difficulty, night — time is recorded but never rated), a performance score and a paged history. The after-action report shows the round's complexity and score.
**WEAPONS PACK** add-on (SCAR-L, M-16, AK-74, AKS-74U) behind the durable SKU `weapons_pack_1`; locked cards open Meta's checkout.
**Menus:** Scenario Mode's room lists are picture cards in sections like the Build menu; the round-setup options cards are redesigned with ON/OFF switches; the BUILD & BREACH logo art leads the home screen and the loading splash.
**Touch Pro controllers** are supported (previously only Touch and Touch Plus).
**Fixes:** NPC rounds no longer leave hit markers in the NPC that fired; RETURN TO EDIT → ABORT no longer lands back on the options card; a squad-session crash on object teardown; a Build-menu error on every scenario click; the PU 3.5x scope is withdrawn; vest ∞ icon removed.
**Release scrub (3.1.28):** Bluetooth permission removed (Meta certification); the tutorial no longer changes the saved VOICE COMMANDS setting; the training record no longer lists the newest run twice; the voice model recovers from an interrupted first unpack; room counting no longer hitches the round; thumbnails no longer leak memory; copy cleaned up across the game (start box, gun names, Fish Bowl hit marks, AAR labels).

# Build & Breach 3.1.19 — release notes

**3.1.19** rolls up everything since 3.1.4: smarter cover shooters and hiders, NPC voices, a darker night, better-looking guns in NPC hands, and a redesigned Build menu.

**People talk:**
- New voices, with jaw movement, for the civilians, the soldiers and the security guard. They take turns and speak about half as often as before.
- The soldier voice is used only for soldiers and the guard, and only when they're hostile.
- Only people in front of you answer voice commands.
- New command: **"Come out"** brings hiders out with their hands up.
- New setting: **NPC VOICES** (on by default) turns their speech off.
**Cover shooters:**
  - They take cover once, behind a real wall or piece of furniture that's between them and you. They never use people as cover, and they sit a little off the wall.
  - They move only if you flank them or hit their cover.
  - With no cover nearby, they stand and fight.
  - They move 20% slower, with no spinning while ducked.
**Hiders:** no more freezing or running in place, and they now hide behind low furniture too.
**NPC weapons:**
  - Pistols and rifles are held with both hands, at the shoulder, with magazines in.
  - Their head and eyes follow the target.
  - The support hand meets the pistol out in front of the body.
  - Soldiers have their own rifle size, stance and grip.
  - NPC gunshots are twice as loud and use a dedicated rifle sound.
**Night:**
  - Night vision is darker, with more contrast and lighter shadows (still darker than lit areas).
  - With goggles up, the house is much darker.
  - Moonlight casts real shadows, and unaided hostiles are nearly blind in the dark.
  - Scopes use the night-vision colours.
**Flashlight:** a clean, full circle on walls and furniture.
**Grenade:** no flash or shake through walls, and no puff when the lever flies.
**Build menu:**
  - Walls, doors, furniture and rooms are sorted into sections of big picture cards with readable names.
  - The NPC list has one behavior picker pinned at the top and bigger rows.
  - The instructions are rewritten so every line fits.
**Cast:** soldiers Frank, Greg and Fiona and security guard Hank join the roster. Cover shooters use a proper rifle cover animation set.
**Loadout:**
  - The LPVO on Picatinny rifles and the PU 3.5x on the AKs are magnified optics.
  - The duplicate flashlight and laser are gone.
**After Action Report:** the rifle ghost stays where the rifle fell.
**Random houses:** room count scales with the area, and cover is placed better.
**Squad play:** needs every player on 3.1.19.

# Build & Breach 3.1.4 — release notes

**3.1.4:**

**Night vision is in the loadout:**
  - Choose OFF, GREEN or WHITE. A colour makes every round a night mission: the house goes dark and the goggles come down at each countdown, in every Fish Bowl round.
  - Grip at your forehead with a free hand to flip the goggles up or down. A white outline on your hand shows when you're in the right spot.
  - With the goggles up the house is very dark, but walls and furniture stay visible. Your weapon light and laser still work.
  - Night vision now costs far less performance.
**Sharper people:**
  - They notice you when any part of them is exposed, not just their eyes.
  - Voice commands work with just an arm showing.
  - When one person reacts, others in the same open room go alert. Closed doors still block everything except gunshots.
**Fish Bowl deals the full cast:** riflemen, cover shooters, hiders and frightened people all turn up regularly on ELITE.
**Start box:**
  - Fish Bowl places it farther from walls.
  - It's now placeable in Build mode (FURNITURE › Start Box). The round waits until you stand on it.

# Build & Breach 3.1.3 — release notes

**3.1.3** smooths how people surrender and where they stand:

**Hands stay up:** someone who already has their hands up keeps them up when you say "hands up" again or tell them to get down or on the ground. No more dropping their hands and raising them again.
**Stepping off walls:** people take a small step away from a wall before they raise their hands, kneel, aim or stop on patrol, so arms and guns don't poke through it. They never step through a doorway, out of your sight, or into someone else.
**Rifle optics:** the micro red dot and RMR are no longer offered as optics on primary weapons.
**Squad play:** needs every player on 3.1.3.

# Build & Breach 3.1.2 — release notes

**3.1.2** fixes the most serious issues from a code review of 3.1.x.

**Squad version check:**
  - Players on different versions can no longer join each other and then drop mid-session. Both sides now get a clear "update Build & Breach to join" message.
  - Online squads are also tagged by version.
**Hiders** run all the way to their corner instead of stopping half a metre short.
**Cowering hiders** have a crouched-size hit box. Shots over their heads no longer count as civilian hits.
**Squad players** no longer see a rifle on an unarmed person.
**"Turn around and face me"** no longer makes people turn away first.
**Grenade pin:** the hand holding your gun can no longer pull it by accident. The pull starts with a fresh squeeze at the ring.
**Scar-L, Tactical Laser and LS321:** network IDs corrected, so squad players see the right model.

# Build & Breach 3.1.1 — release notes

**3.1.1** fixes issues found testing 3.1.0 on the headset:

**Closed doors and walls block NPC senses:**
  - People behind a closed door no longer react before you open it: nothing gets through, whether proximity, the room-wide alert or voice commands.
  - "Hands up" people now raise their hands when they SEE you, not at the start of the round.
  - Gunshots still carry through walls.
**AAR gun ghost:** now a full-size copy of the gun you held, with its optic, laser, light, suppressor and magazine. The loose parts and the tiny extra gun are gone.
**Night vision:** about 10% darker. Laser and flashlight glows sit on the lens instead of floating in front of it, and the laser dot bloom sits on the wall.
**Micro red dot** now fits the M4 (MK18), Scar-L and MP5 on a riser, at the same height as the holo. The M16A1 has no rail, so it still takes no optic.

# Build & Breach 3.1.0 — release notes

**3.1.0** is the biggest update since 3.0: a new cast of people, voice commands, a loadout builder, the frag grenade and a rebuilt night vision.

**New NPCs:** ten new realistic adult characters (five men, five women) replace the old cast. Rooms saved with the old characters still load and get the nearest new one.
**New behaviors, picked by category** (HOSTILE / INNOCENT / FAKE SURRENDER):
  - Hands Up: already surrendered, in varied poses.
  - Hider: runs for a corner or furniture and cowers.
  - Cover Shooter: fights from cover and peeks to shoot.
  - Rifleman: starts with a rifle in both hands.
**Voice commands** (offline, on the headset): "hands up", "get down / on the ground", "don't move", "police", "turn around" and "face me".
  - Innocents in your line of sight obey.
  - People get down facing you: prone if there's room, kneeling if not. Anyone kneeling stays down.
  - The AAR shows your commands.
  - The microphone permission is asked at launch.
**Loadout builder:**
  - Pick a primary and a secondary from picture lists.
  - Fit each one's attachments. Primaries have OPTIC, LASER, LIGHT and MUZZLE, so a laser and a light can go on together.
  - Turn the grenade on or off.
  - Your loadout is saved across restarts.
**Laser and light controls:** laser on the support hand's Y/B, light on the support hand's trigger.
**Frag grenade** (SETTINGS > GRENADES, off by default):
  - One M67 on the vest. Grab it, pull the pin with your other hand, then throw.
  - The blast goes through drywall and wood like a bullet but is stopped by masonry, and it can kill you.
  - Fragment wounds show as orange rods on the NPC's AAR ghost.
**NPC movement:**
  - Runners no longer stick in walls or freeze. They turn before they run and replan when blocked.
  - In a tight space they cower where they are.
  - Surrendered people can't be shoved along, and nobody fires while moving.
**Night vision:** the whole scene now goes monochrome in both green and white phosphor, including walls, guns and people. It stays correct when turned on back to back. Lasers and lights are in the night-vision look straight away.
**Also:**
  - A smaller, more accurate player hitbox; your AAR ghost shows where your gun was.
  - A held rifle no longer catches on the mags on your vest.
  - Original gun audio is back, and the MK18 and MP5 have their suppressors again.

Build & Breach 3.0.1

Fix: the intro tutorial now runs with the room scan switched off, even on a headset that has scanned its room. The tutorial stages its rooms in front of you, and the real walls were hiding them and blocking their NPCs. Your saved room-scan setting is untouched and comes back the moment the tutorial ends.

Also removed a one-time "move this menu" pop-up that could appear out of view on the home screen.

No other changes from 3.0.0.

Build & Breach 3.0.0 — the first full release.

DOORS: A new door that follows your hand exactly, swings with real momentum and latches shut. Grab the knob (it lights up as you reach for it) to pull a door open or push it closed. Doors hold their frame after a headset doff, and NPCs use doorways you open.

HIT MARKERS: Rods now trace the true flight line of every round, on standing and downed targets alike. A downed threat keeps only the shots that dropped it. Wall hits leave a clean X: green in a scoring zone, red on a miss.

LIGHTING: Walls, doors and NPCs cast shadows onto your real floor.

TRAINING: A guided first session covers controller orientation, a full load-fire-holster drill and five rooms. The WEAPONS tab now tours all eight guns, and every on-screen instruction matches how the guns really work.

WEAPONS: Eight-gun loadout: Glock, MK18, MP5, SCAR-L, M16, AK-74, AKS-74U and the Model 1897 shotgun. Support grips keep your controller out of the sight picture. Shotgun pump, AK safety and brass ejection all fixed.

PERFORMANCE: Foveated rendering, background navmesh baking, a 45% smaller download. 72 fps in every session we measured.

ALSO: Clean round-to-round resets, fake surrenders grade correctly, hostiles no longer give themselves away with a draw sound, and Instructor-Led connects to Sentari Command only when you choose.
